chapter_theme: The opening of Madurai Valaisami's Njanak Kummi: four invocatory stanzas (the guru, the maiden goddess, the Vel of Senthil and the Vinayaka of the root triangle), then the cosmology of the kummi told as a village estate. The one great void is a city; its lord is a mute Siddha, and the lady who speaks for him builds the town, lays down its law and farms earth and sky; five villages divided five by five grow from one seed; and a cast of tenants, headmen, an accountant, a Brahmin, a merchant, agents and servants hold shares in the land. Each is a coded element, faculty or tattva of the body, and the refrain asks the 'jnana girl' whether she can see the justice of their claims.
structure_note: 2518 to 2521 are the kaappu stanzas, one to each guardian; 2522 to 2523 announce the subject (tattva, the body as a vessel of filth, yoga as Tamil song); 2524 to 2528 set out the void-city, the mute lord and the lady who rules; 2529 to 2542 enumerate the estate's villages, hill and shareholders. From 2522 every stanza ends with the refrain ஞானப்பெண்ணே.

2518.reading: By the grace of the true guru, the Paradesi whose form is excellent jnana, Ganapati the child of Siva is the guard for singing the Njanak Kummi upon the rock.
2518.nuance: பரதேசிகன் (Paradesi, the wandering renunciant) is the guru's title; the singer credits the song to his grace before any god. பாறமீதின் (upon the rock) may be literal, a place of singing, or the firm ground of the practice.

2519.reading: Praising the feet of Ambika the Maiden, to sing in Tamil the kummi of grace-bliss, Siva's Subramaniya, brother of the elephant-faced one, is the guard.
2519.nuance: The goddess is invoked as வாலை, the maiden, which is also the singer's own name (Valaisami); the whole kummi is addressed to a 'jnana girl', so the maiden is at once deity, poet and listener.

2520.reading: Praising on high him who stood as the fourth Veda, as the six, and as the many different distinctions, to sing the kummi, the feet of the Vel-bearer of Senthil are the guard.
2520.nuance: ஓராறு (the six) is unglossed: the six Vedangas, the six shastras or the six adharas are all possible. நானாபேதம் (many distinctions) makes the god the ground of all differences, a theme the next stanzas take up.

2521.reading: For the kummi that Valaisami of high Madurai sings, the feet of the Vinayaka of the root triangle at the base of Meru are the guard.
2521.nuance: The poet names himself and his city. மேருவதன் அடி மூல முக்கோணம் (the root triangle at the foot of Meru) is the yogic body: tradition takes Meru as the spine and the triangle as the muladhara, where Ganapati presides; 2584 returns to the 'root Ganapati'.

2522.reading: Beginning and end becoming one, growing as the two, the cosmos and the body, and standing as many different kinds: hear the tattva of this, jnana girl.
2522.nuance: அண்ட பிரண்டம் is the Siddhars' pair அண்டம் and பிண்டம், the world and the body, here the first division of the undivided one. சாதி (kinds) is the many classes of beings, and may carry its social sense of caste as a product of the same differentiation.

2523.reading: The body is a vessel of filth; the subtle thing that comes into it, and its origin, are the matter of this Tamil song called yoga: hear it with a glad mind, jnana girl.
2523.nuance: சிற்பனம் and உற்பனம் are read as the subtle (சித்) that enters the body and its arising (உற்பத்தி); the forms are irregular. மலபாண்டம் (vessel of filth) is the stock Siddhar figure for the body, used here not to despise it but to introduce what enters it.

2524.reading: The one great void is a city, and in it there is a certain Siddha; he has no mouth to speak the state of the vaasi; and that bridegroom is a woman, jnana girl.
2524.nuance: ஏகப்பெருவெளி (the one great expanse) is the supreme space, told as a city. The mute Siddha within it is tradition's Siva as witness; that the bridegroom 'is a woman' makes the lord and his Shakti one, which 2525 and 2526 develop. வாசநிலை may be the state of breath (வாசி) or of dwelling (வாசம்).

2525.reading: For Brahma called the witness, the child, a root ... became a woman; she stands as the ground of the two, the subtle and the causal, and says 'we are the gross', jnana girl.
2525.nuance: The third line has lost its opening syllables, so the pair ending in ...சும காரணம் is restored as சூக்கும (subtle) and காரண (causal), the three bodies with தூலம் (gross). On that reading Shakti is the ground of the subtle and causal and declares herself the gross; the witness-Brahma is the still consciousness. பகைத்தி is unclear.

2526.reading: She knew him to be mute, and says 'all that mute one's speech is us'; she organised herself to rule the country; that is the great lady, jnana girl.
2526.nuance: The lord is silent and the lady speaks and governs: the Shakta picture in which all activity, speech included, is Shakti's and Siva is the unspeaking ground. சங்கட்டினாள் (organised, arranged) is read from சங்கற்பம் or from a dialect verb; it is uncertain.

2527.reading: The ruby that is queen of women: is there even any hearing of her being called a woman? Hear the way by which she joined earth and sky and raised a crop, jnana girl.
2527.nuance: The goddess is beyond the word 'woman' even as she is the queen of women. The crop raised by joining earth and sky is the stock cipher for creation, the body in the cosmos; the estate-and-farming figure of the rest of the chapter begins here.

2528.reading: The great queen built a town and, with her lord, framed the law of its administration in good order; telling it would never end, so hear a little of the seed, jnana girl.
2528.nuance: The 'law' (அதிகாரச் சட்டம்) is the ordering of the created world and the body, told in the idiom of a landed estate; விதை (seed) announces that what follows is a condensed account of its origin.

2529.reading: It became a division of five villages; within it there came to be five-times-five parts; for the five villages there was one seed; and for that there is a tank, jnana girl.
2529.nuance: The arithmetic is cipher: tradition reads the five villages as the five elements, the twenty-five as their fivefold products (the five-times-five tattvas of Siddhar reckoning), the one seed as bindu and the tank as the womb or the water of the body. ஆணகுளம் is unclear, 'the male tank' or 'the fitting tank'.

2530.reading: Next to the village there is also a hill; those stationed within it are the holders of posts; hear now as their names are told, and what their greatness is, jnana girl.
2530.nuance: The hill beside the village is, in the Siddhar body-map, the head above the trunk (Meru, 2521). The 'stationed men' who are named in the following stanzas are the faculties and powers lodged there; the names are place-puns and the readings below give them as tradition would, not as settled.

2531.reading: That Sattaiyappillai who lives at Thalaimannar is tall; she asked what is sin and what is tax-free grant; do you know the truth of it, jnana girl?
2531.nuance: தலைமன்னார் puns on தலை (head): the tall one who lives in the head may be the breath or the intellect. பாவம் and மானியம் (sin, and land held free of tax) set deeds and their exemption against each other; the question is whether anything in the body is exempt from karma.

2532.reading: Appu Pillai at Kumbakonam came asking for a half share, saying that if his gathering fails there is great distress; how is the justice of this to be settled, jnana girl?
2532.nuance: கும்பகோணம் carries கும்பம் (the pot, the head or the held breath of kumbhaka); அப்பு is also the element water. One reading is the breath or the water-element claiming its half of the body's produce; the stanza gives only the claim and the question.

2533.reading: Have the five Vanni gods of the root household fierceness, resolve and a path? They say 'the share of the four banks is ours'; do you know the justice of this, jnana girl?
2533.nuance: வன்னி is fire, and the five fire-gods of the root household are read as the five fires or the fiery powers at the muladhara (மூலக்குடி); the four banks they claim may be the four other elements or the four directions. The stanza queries their claim rather than granting it.

2534.reading: For Katthavaraya the undivided one there is the guarding of the directions and all other inquiry; 'we are the ones who see to it', they say; will this state hold, jnana girl?
2534.nuance: காத்தவராயன் is the village guardian deity, here a figure for whatever guards the body's eight directions, which tradition gives to the eight siddhis or the directional gods. The text of lines 2 and 3 (விசாரணை பும், நாமென்கிற ரீந்தப்) is damaged and the reading is approximate.

2535.reading: The supreme light that is space says that the share of the five banks is gathered within himself; hear this news, jnana girl.
2535.nuance: The one shareholder whose claim the song reports without challenge: the light that is space (the fifth element, and beyond it the inner space) holds the five, taken as the five elements, within itself. This is the pervasion doctrine in the estate idiom.

2536.reading: The hall-men are three, and besides there is one head-accountant of the forest; if they make trouble, do you know the way the former's order runs, jnana girl?
2536.nuance: அம்பலக்காரர் are the village headmen; three of them may be the three gunas or the three malas. மஸ்தக காட்டுக் கணக்கன் carries மஸ்தகம் (the head): an accountant in the head is tradition's reckoning faculty (buddhi or chitta). The stanza asks what rule governs them when they rebel.

2537.reading: Nine dancers are also shareholders, and in which village their villages lie is the way of it; and for the fifty who are the clerks there is one elder brother, jnana girl.
2537.nuance: The nine dancers are read as the nine gates or the nine planets; the fifty (ஐம்பதி, with the garbled சேருவைக்காரர்) suggest the fifty letters with their one 'elder brother', Om. Line 2 (ஊருக்குளூர்களூமய்படியாம்) is corrupt and the reading is tentative.

2538.reading: The priest at Serai is a Brahmin, and his house is above the raft-tank; leaping about he slaps his thigh in challenge; will the land go to him, hear, jnana girl?
2538.nuance: The Brahmin above the tank who struts and claims the land is one more shareholder whose claim is questioned; one reading is the ego or the ritual mind lodged above the water of the body. The stanza is satire of priestly claims as well as cipher.

2539.reading: A merchant too is a shareholder; the one who joined there grew very great; if he brings the bound-up gold coin, will his title to the land stand, jnana girl?
2539.nuance: The Chetti who tries to buy the body's land with hoarded coin (வராகன்) is read as desire or acquisitiveness; the song asks whether wealth gives any claim on the self. The stanza's claimants form a series of 'will it hold?' questions.

2540.reading: The agents are five; to oversee their work there are twice five; the sorcerers of samadhi are three; hear the word, jnana girl.
2540.nuance: Five, ten and three are the standard counts of the senses, the ten organs of sense and action (or the ten airs) and the three (gunas or states). மாரீசக்காரர் (men of Maricha, the shape-shifting demon) makes the three 'of samadhi' deceivers, perhaps the three states that counterfeit absorption.

2541.reading: The servants are many, and they have plentiful stipend and wages; but if a ladder is set against the pot-fort, they will hide, jnana girl.
2541.nuance: பானையங்கோட்டை, the fort that is a pot, is the body or the skull; the many well-paid servants who vanish when it is scaled are the faculties that fail at death or in the yogi's ascent. Both readings keep the point that the body's retainers cannot be relied on.

2542.reading: For the void-form there is one superintendent, and if you look at him he seems a small boy; the man of Velur sells off his own half share, jnana girl.
2542.nuance: The child-like overseer of the void (பாழுரு) recalls the Siddhars' child-god, Murugan or the ever-young Lord, who is tiny to look at and master of everything. The Velur man who sells his half share is unexplained; the ellipsis of the stanza is deliberate cipher.

links.note: Pattinathar does not know the sign of the form the Lord took as atom within atom in all the cosmos and the body; Valaisami opens his tattva with the one growing as the two, cosmos and body, and then as many kinds. Both make அண்டம் and பிண்டம் the first division of the one.

The Naladiyar's body is a pot seeping filth from nine openings that only a fool calls beautiful; Valaisami's body is a vessel of filth too, but he names it only to ask what subtle thing enters it and where that comes from. The same image serves disgust in one and inquiry in the other.

Pattinathar's picture 'matching ten and eight, two fives, thirteen, two and one' and Valaisami's five villages divided five by five from one seed both give the tattvas as a number-cipher the hearer must decode; neither names a single tattva.

Tirumular places fire, water, air, sun, moon and the gods all within the heart; Valaisami's space-light says the share of the five is gathered within himself. In both the elements are held inside one inner principle rather than outside the body.

source_issues: 2525: line 3 begins with an ellipsis (...சுமகாரணமிரண்டினுக்கு); the opening syllables are lost in the source.
2532: the stanza ends with a stray comma after ஞானப்பெண்ணே.
2534: lines 2 and 3 are damaged (விசாரணை பும், நாமென்கிற ரீந்தப்).
2537: line 2 (ஊருக்குளூர்களூமய்படியாம்) is garbled; ஐம்பதி சேருவைக்காரர் in line 3 is also doubtful.
2518 to 2521 are kaappu stanzas without the refrain; the refrain ஞானப்பெண்ணே begins at 2522.
